mcq.q: If r = -0.9, σx = 20 and σy = 14, the covariance between x and y is:
mcq.explain: From r = cov/(σx σy): cov = r × σx × σy = -0.9 × 20 × 14 = -252. Covariance carries the units of x times the units of y, while r has no units. A negative r gives a negative covariance.
mcq.topic: Karl Pearson's product moment correlation coefficient
mcq.fast: Covariance = r × σx × σy (multiply all three).

mcq.q: If the regression coefficients are byx = -0.9 and bxy = -0.4, the correlation coefficient r is:
mcq.explain: r² = byx × bxy = -0.9 × -0.4 = 0.36, so |r| = 0.6. r takes the common sign of the two regression coefficients, which are both negative: r = -0.6. Their arithmetic mean is always at least |r|.
mcq.topic: Properties of regression coefficients and lines
mcq.fast: r = ±√(byx × bxy), sign of the coefficients.

mcq.q: Given r = -0.4, σx = 11 and σy = 12, find byx (the slope of the regression of y on x).
mcq.explain: byx = r × σy/σx and bxy = r × σx/σy. Here byx = -0.4 × 12/11 = -0.4364. The SD of the dependent variable goes on top. Swapping the SDs gives the other coefficient.
mcq.topic: Properties of regression coefficients and lines
mcq.fast: byx = r × (σ of the dependent variable ÷ σ of the other).

mcq.topic: Properties of regression coefficients and lines
mcq.fast: bxy = r × (σ of the dependent variable ÷ σ of the other).

mcq.q: The two regression lines are 3x − y − 49 = 0 and 5x + 3y − 77 = 0. The means of x and y are:
mcq.explain: Both regression lines pass through the point of means (x̄, ȳ). So solve the two equations together: x = 16, y = -1. Check: 3(16) + -1(-1) + -49 = 0 and 5(16) + 3(-1) + -77 = 0. It does not matter which line is y on x for this question.
mcq.topic: Properties of regression coefficients and lines
mcq.fast: Solve the two lines simultaneously (or substitute each option pair).

mcq.q: The two regression lines are −4x + 5y + 15 = 0 and 20x − 9y − 300 = 0. The coefficient of correlation is:
mcq.explain: Try taking one line as y on x and the other as x on y; the product of the two slopes must not exceed 1. The valid choice gives byx = 0.8 and bxy = 0.45, so r² = 0.36 and r = 0.6 (same sign as the coefficients). The wrong assignment gives a product of 2.78, which is above 1 and therefore impossible.
mcq.topic: Properties of regression coefficients and lines
mcq.fast: Multiply the candidate slopes; if the product exceeds 1, swap which line is y on x.

mcq.q: For 9 pairs of ranks, Σd² = 198. Spearman's rank correlation coefficient is about:
mcq.explain: R = 1 − 6Σd²/[n(n² − 1)] = 1 − 6 × 198/[9(81 − 1)] = 1 − 1188/720 = -0.65. Using n² + 1 in the denominator, or forgetting to subtract from 1, are the usual slips. R lies between −1 and +1.
mcq.topic: Spearman's rank correlation and concurrent deviations
mcq.fast: Spearman R = 1 − 6Σd² ÷ (n³ − n).

mcq.q: For the data x: 5, 10, 7, 1, 2 and y: -9, -11, -6, -5, -5, Karl Pearson's coefficient of correlation is about:
mcq.explain: x̄ = 5, ȳ = -7.2. Σ(x − x̄)(y − ȳ) = -32, Σ(x − x̄)² = 54, Σ(y − ȳ)² = 28.8. r = -32/√(54 × 28.8) ≈ -0.811. The slope Σxy/Σx² (-0.593) is the regression coefficient, not r.
mcq.topic: Karl Pearson's product moment correlation coefficient
mcq.fast: Use deviations from the means in a three-column table: dx·dy, dx², dy².

mcq.q: For the data x: 9, 12, 13, 4, 10 and y: 18, 21, 27, 7, 17, Karl Pearson's coefficient of correlation is about:
mcq.explain: x̄ = 9.6, ȳ = 18. Σ(x − x̄)(y − ȳ) = 99, Σ(x − x̄)² = 49.2, Σ(y − ȳ)² = 212. r = 99/√(49.2 × 212) ≈ 0.969. The slope Σxy/Σx² (2.012) is the regression coefficient, not r.
mcq.topic: Karl Pearson's product moment correlation coefficient
mcq.fast: Use deviations from the means in a three-column table: dx·dy, dx², dy².

mcq.q: If r = 0.9, the percentage of variation in y explained by x (coefficient of determination) is:
mcq.explain: Coefficient of determination = r² = (0.9)² = 0.81, i.e. 81% of the variation in y is explained by x. It is never negative, even when r is negative, because it is a square. The remaining share is due to other factors.
mcq.topic: Coefficient of determination and spurious correlation
mcq.fast: Square r, then multiply by 100 for the percentage.

mcq.q: x̄ = 19, ȳ = 80, σx = 9, σy = 10 and r = -0.5. Using the regression of y on x, the estimate of y when x = 25 is:
mcq.explain: Regression of y on x: y − ȳ = byx(x − x̄), with byx = r σy/σx = -0.5 × 10/9 = -0.56. So y = 80 + -0.56 × (25 − 19) = 76.67. Using bxy here would estimate x from y instead.
mcq.topic: Regression and the method of least squares
mcq.fast: Estimate ŷ = ȳ + r(σy/σx)(x − x̄).

mcq.q: In a series of 10 pairs of observations, the number of concurrent deviations is 5. The coefficient of concurrent deviation is about:
mcq.explain: With n = 10 pairs there are m = n − 1 = 9 deviations. rc = ±√[±(2c − m)/m] = ±√[±(2 × 5 − 9)/9] = ±√[±(1)/9]. The inner value is positive, so both signs are +: rc ≈ 0.3333. Using n instead of m = n − 1 is a common slip.
mcq.topic: Spearman's rank correlation and concurrent deviations
mcq.fast: m = n − 1; rc = ±√(|2c − m|/m) with the sign of (2c − m).

mcq.q: In a series of 19 pairs of observations, the number of concurrent deviations is 0. The coefficient of concurrent deviation is about:
mcq.explain: With n = 19 pairs there are m = n − 1 = 18 deviations. rc = ±√[±(2c − m)/m] = ±√[±(2 × 0 − 18)/18] = ±√[±(-18)/18]. The inner value is negative, so both signs are −: rc ≈ -1.0000. Using n instead of m = n − 1 is a common slip.
mcq.topic: Spearman's rank correlation and concurrent deviations
mcq.fast: m = n − 1; rc = ±√(|2c − m|/m) with the sign of (2c − m).
